content.title: About
content.content: Kale (Brassica oleracea var. sabellica) is a leafy vegetable known for its high levels of vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants. When boiled (about 5‑7 minutes) most nutrients are retained and the texture becomes tender, making it suitable for soups, purees, and side dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Kale is often called a “superfood” because of its dense nutrient profile.
Ancient Roman varieties were cultivated, and it became popular throughout medieval Europe.
Leaves can be green, purple, or variegated depending on the cultivar.
Kale is frost‑tolerant and can continue growing in sub‑zero temperatures.
In Japan, kale is known as “katsuka” and is used in traditional dishes.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Kale provides over 700% of the daily value for vitamin K, essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Abundant antioxidants
items.content: Kale contains carotenoids, quercetin, and other polyphenols that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Source of calcium and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are important for bone, muscle, and nerve function.

items.title: Low‑calorie protein and fiber
items.content: Kale contributes plant protein and dietary fiber, promoting satiety and digestive health.

items.title: Interaction with blood thinners
items.content: High vitamin K intake may reduce the effectiveness of anticoagulant medications.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Kale contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Rarely, some people may experience an allergy to cruciferous vegetables.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled kale can be added to soups, stews, salads, served as a side dish with meat or fish, or blended into a puree. Before cooking, rinse the leaves well and remove thick stems.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh kale in the refrigerator in a bag or container with a slight moisture for up to 5 days. Cooked kale should be stored in an airtight container in the fridge for no more than 3‑4 days.
